title: Circuit Detour Orchestrator for per-model & customer-domain trip policies
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Design and implement a Circuit Detour Orchestrator (CDO) that enforces per-dependency, per-model, and per-customer-domain trip thresholds with automated detour routing to safe alternatives. Goal is to keep SLOs stable under dependency degradation by steering traffic to verified detour paths (model variants, cached responses, regional replicas) while preserving correctness constraints and minimizing cost.
acceptance_criteria: CDO supports three scope levels: dependency, model, and customer_domain with independent thresholds and hysteresis.
Detour actions include: model-variant switch, regional reroute, cached prefix response, and degraded-response template.
On-trip, CDO logs a deterministic reason code and emits traces + metrics: trip_reason, scope, pre_trip_qps, post_detour_qps, error_rate_delta.
Canary rollout to 10% traffic for a customer_domain and automatic rollback if error_rate increases >0.5% over baseline within 15m.
Playbook + runbook added to Console with a one-click manual override and circuit-inspection view.
implementation_notes: Introduce a new detour-policy proto stored in config-service. Policy includes trip_metric, window_ms, threshold, hysteresis_multiplier, min_traffic, allowed_detours.
Trip decision will be computed in the routing mesh (edge) using aggregated rolling windows to avoid cross-region amplification.
Default safety margin: hysteresis_multiplier=1.5 and cooldown=5m, overridable per-customer-domain for enterprise contracts.
Detour candidates ranked by correctness score then cost. Correctness score computed from previous evals and unit tests run during model onboarding.
Shadowed dry-run mode for 48h to collect telemetry before any active detour. Dry-run emits detour_suggestion events to the metrics pipeline.
tradeoffs: Strongly conservative trips reduce blast radius but may degrade latency/cost; policy defaults favor SLO stability over unit-cost optimization.
Centralized config allows ownership and compliance but increases control-plane dependency risk; mitigate via local cached policies with TTL.
Evaluating correctness at routing time adds CPU overhead—mitigated by precomputed correctness tiers and simple rank lookup.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Dry-run): enable shadowed decisions for 100% traffic for 2 regions (us-west/us-east) for 48h.
Phase 1 (Canary): active detours for 10% traffic for a small customer cohort, monitor SLO and error delta for 1 week.
Phase 2 (Regional Rollout): expand to all regions with per-region tuning and autoscaling knobs for detour bandwidth.
Phase 3 (GA): enable global default policies and surface UI controls in Console for customer-domain overrides.
metrics_to_monitor: SLO: latency_p99 and success_rate per-customer_domain and per-model
trip_rate: number of trips per minute and per dependency
post_detour_delta: change in error_rate and latency after detour
false_positive_rate: proportion of dry-run detour suggestions that would have hurt correctness
cost_delta: additional GPU-hours or token cost attributable to detours
